facts.F16: A1: the platform lane membership is measured from the IL and fixed in a namespace-agnostic test that fails when a listed type is missing or a listed name does not exist, finds no domain-event handler outside Modules, and records the suppression and analyser-config targets naming moving types.
facts.F17: The move in feature B has a fixed, measured list of what moves, where, and what stays with which owner
facts.F18: A2: every rule pattern gives the same answer for each moving platform type under its old and its new namespace, no added alternative matches a production type outside Platform, and no rule string names a moving area by its old path.
facts.F19: No rule silently stops seeing a platform type when it moves
facts.F2: The platform types can move to Platform/ without any rule, CI selection or answer silently changing
facts.F20: A3: a change to Platform/Releases/GitHubService.cs or its test path selects the GitHub live suite, and the existing classifier cases keep their selection.
facts.F21: The live GitHub suite still runs when the release code moves
facts.F22: A4: the platform-answers-compare examine command says DIFFERENT (exit 1) for two captures differing in one answer, IDENTICAL (exit 0) for identical ones, and fails when nothing was compared.
facts.F23: A changed platform answer after the move is caught at EXAMINE
facts.F3: The membership of the platform lane is measured from the compiled code and fixed in a test: each platform type with its area, its old and its new namespace, and the files that stay with their owner; the test finds each listed type in its old or its new namespace, fails when a listed type is missing or a listed name does not exist, finds no domain-event handler outside Modules, and records every suppression or analyser-config target that names a moving type.
facts.F4: Every rule pattern in the test assembly gives the same answer for each moving platform type under its new Platform namespace as under its old one, and no added alternative matches a production type outside Platform; the inline DomainEvents fragment is replaced by the exact dispatcher type.
facts.F5: No string in the rule files names a moving area (Encryption, DatabaseManagement, UsageData, Logging, DomainEvents, BackgroundServices.Update, Interfaces.Update) or a moving loose type by its old Services.Implementation, Services.Interfaces or Services/Implementation path, except the entries the membership list names as renamed by a move slice.
facts.F6: A change to Platform/Releases/GitHubService.cs, or to its test path, selects the GitHub live suite in CI test selection, and every path the classifier already handled keeps its selection.
facts.F7: A platform-answers-compare examine command, declared in .nwave/examine.json before any file moves, compares the platform answers of two revisions (system info, version without the GitHub calls, encryption and secrets state, database-management status, usage-data state, log level and problems, update status; volatile fields dropped) and says DIFFERENT with exit 1 when one answer changed, IDENTICAL with exit 0 when none did, and fails when nothing was compared.
facts.F8: Nothing a user, a tracker or the database sees changes: no production file moves or changes behaviour in feature A, and every existing test stays green.
facts.F9: The IL-measured platform lane membership map (types, areas, old and new namespaces, files that stay with owner, suppression and analyser-config targets naming moving types); the preservation law over every const regex in the test assembly with the widening it requires, the dispatcher fragment made exact, and the old-path literal check; the GitHub live-suite selection for Platform/Releases in path-classifier.sh; the platform-answers-compare examine command and its declaration in .nwave/examine.json.
